correctness.rationale: Two holes in one blade obstruct each other permanently: every possible sender to either sees both. With one hole in each of t blades there are binom(k,t)m^t labelled choices. With the hub seeded, t=0 succeeds, t=1 requires beta<=U, and t>=2 requires beta<=L. Without the hub, t=k cannot start; t=0 requires beta<=H; 2<=t<k requires beta<=L, which also guarantees the hub first fills. For t=1, the hub receives A=m(k-1)alpha in round one, and the last hole receives L+alpha A in round two. It received nothing in round one, and any no-fill round terminates the process, so cumulative weights do not supply an uncounted later opportunity. The hub retains its full received weight, not beta. Thus both inequalities at T=min(A,L+alpha A) are inclusive. Summing binom(k,t)m^t z^(N-t) or z^(N-1-t) over these cases gives exactly the two polynomials; L<T<=H and U<=H yield the four minimum-size regimes. For alpha=1/(4mk) the jump k-2 is realized for k>=3. The minimum-multiplicity example starts at 2^4+4*2^3=48 in the low-threshold regime; the rest follows from the one- and two-hole coefficients. The supplied exact-rational verifier was inspected, not run; its stated 337 instances do not prove the theorem.
